name: Angela Rayner
role: British Labour politician: MP for Ashton-under-Lyne since 2015, Deputy Leader of the Labour Party 2020-25, Deputy Prime Minister 2024-25, Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
summary: Rayner's Commons record shows a Labour left-of-centre MP who voted against assisted dying and Trident renewal, for the Employment Rights Bill and against minimum service levels for strikes, and for ending hereditary peers' seats.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: On 15 October 2024 she voted No on the Conservative reasoned amendment that would have declined to give the House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Bill a second reading, which fell 105 to 453, so supporting the removal of the remaining hereditary peers' seats.

assisted-dying.rationale: She voted No on the second reading of the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill on 29 November 2024 (330-275) and No on its third reading on 20 June 2025 (314-291).

decide-locally.rationale: Introducing the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill on 2 September 2025, she said that 'from top to bottom, the best decisions for communities are made by those who know their area best', and that the Bill gives local communities a bigger say through neighbourhood governance and a community right to buy.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: On 18 July 2016 she voted No on the motion supporting renewal of the UK's nuclear deterrent, which passed 472 to 117.

unions-good.rationale: She voted Aye on the second reading of the Employment Rights Bill (21 October 2024, 386-105), which widens union rights, and No on the third reading of the Strikes (Minimum Service Levels) Bill (30 January 2023, 315-246).

notes: A first audit from her recorded Commons votes, read from the division lists in the local Hansard corpus (about 1,600 divisions since 2015; searched by theme: assisted dying, Trident, Brexit, strikes and trade unions, immigration, the Employment Rights Bill, hereditary peers). Five statements answered; the votes are medium at most. Her Commons speeches (2024-26, searched by theme: right to buy, rents, leasehold, devolution, water, workers' rights) add decide-locally; the rest state no position that settles a statement beyond the votes. Many statements stay null and the uncertainty rule is not met.
